text:
arjun: quick heads-up  onboarding nova-lite-5b (hf -> redwood int4). FP16 looks fine but int4 produces subtle word-shift errors and punctuation dropout on multi-sentence prompts.
lina: how subtle? any quick metrics?
arjun: yes. SummEval fluency FP16 4.02 -> int4 2.53; token-shift rate ~22% around sentence boundaries. small prefixes sometimes drop commas.
matt: smells like rotary frequency or phase scaling mismatch + tokenizer normalization. nova checkpoints have a per-head `rotary_gamma` tensor (nonstandard name) and a tokenizer that treats U+2018/U+2019 differently. converter likely ignored gamma and we defaulted tokenizer_mode=fast.
lina: if rotary angles are scaled by gamma<1, angles will alias at medium contexts and punctuation tokens get confused. can you repro with a tiny patch that applies per-head gamma when generating sin/cos?
arjun: repro patch I ran locally: after conversion I patched sin/cos generation: for h in range(H): freqs[h] *= meta.get(f"rotary_gamma_{h}", 1.0). Ran microbench of 50 prompts.
arjun: results: fluency 3.95 and token-shift down to 3.5% when gamma applied. without it we were 2.53 and 22%.
zoe: good find. tokenizer issue?
arjun: yes. nova's vocab contains left/right single quotation marks (U+2018/U+2019). HF fast tokenizer normalized them to ASCII apostrophe by default in some builds; the checkpoint expects them as-is. that mismatch creates an ID shadow where two different inputs map to same id or different ids across client/runtime, shifting KV offsets.
lina: so two separate issues: (1) rotary_gamma ignored, (2) tokenizer normalization mismatch. both amplify when combined.
matt: mitigation plan: (A) convert pipeline should read any legacy rotary_gamma* tensors and embed per-head gamma into artifact metadata and apply them when building tables; (B) add a `tokenizer_mode` step in convert that preserves unicode punctuation by default and emits `tokenizer_hash`; (C) add a short autodetect that tries gamma candidates [0.75,0.9,1.0,1.1] and compares microbench ppl/rouge to pick best if present.
zoe: auto-detect algorithm idea: if checkpoint contains rotary_gamma* values, use them; else run quick grid over global gamma multipliers and pick highest avg log-likelihood on 20 micro prompts. also emit chosen gamma vector into metadata (as hex hash) so Console can show it.
arjun: I'll open a PR with: - read rotary_gamma* tensors into artifact; - apply per-head gamma when building sin/cos; - add `--tokenizer_preserve_unicode` flag default true; - emit metadata keys: "rotary_gamma_present" ("true"|"false"), "rotary_gamma_hash", "tokenizer_mode", "tokenizer_hash". target: patch today, full 6-bench run tomorrow night.
lina: add unit test: microbench 20 prompts must recover >95% of FP16 fluency score or fail onboarding. also add a tokenizer smoke that runs a couple of sentences with curly quotes to assert token ids stable between hf-fast and converted artifact if tokenizer_mode==preserve.
matt: one more caveat: when gamma is applied per-head, KV-cache behavior doesn't change but numerical rounding at int4 might. include per-head asymmetric calibration after gamma application. that recovered ~0.3 fluency points in my local run.
arjun: good point  will chain per-head calibration after gamma-adjusted conversion. I'll attach minimal repro and logs in PR.
onboard-bot: created RED-1213: "nova-lite-5b int4 rotary_gamma + tokenizer_unicode mismatch" assigned to arjun.
zoe: Console/ops follow-up: show a warning banner if model.tokenizer_hash != client.tokenizer_hash and link to docs about KV-cache offsets and punctuation quirks.
lina: +1. also ensure converted artifact includes `converter_version` and `conversion_flags` so we can trace back.
arjun: thanks all. PR incoming in ~2 hours, will ping for review and drop microbench logs in the ticket.
